page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supporting AVX, AVX512F, and AVX512_VNNI instruction sets. The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Additionally, it includes a 614 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results position this server primarily in the average tier for general compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores are 1415.19 and 7440.93, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 415.26 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds reach 49.07 GB/sec and 36.25 GB/sec. The server demonstrates average performance in database operations with a PassMark database score of 2904.22 and Redis SET operations at 7.04 million operations per second. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak at 27.55 GB/sec, and medium-sized LLM inference yields poor to weak results, with prompt processing at 14.81 tokens per second and text generation at 7.32 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-8ds_v4 offers a high density of memory and local SSD storage relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require extreme multi-threaded CPU performance. The inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD provides fast temporary storage without requiring external disk attachments. This hardware profile is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data buffering, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring high memory capacity.
